summary.name: LocalSend
summary.one_liner: LocalSend is a free, open-source, cross-platform app for sharing files and text with nearby devices over the local WiFi network without using the internet or cloud.
keywords: share files between android and windows
use_cases: Sending photos or videos between phone and computer
Transferring large files over home or office WiFi
Sharing files across mixed operating systems
Moving files without using cloud storage or accounts
Sending text snippets to nearby devices
summary.what_it_does: LocalSend lets you select files, photos, videos, documents, or text and send them to a nearby device on the same local network. Transfers use your WiFi network and are described as encrypted with HTTPS, with an optional PIN verification step. The page says no account or login is needed and no servers are involved. Files are saved to the device's Downloads folder by default, and the location can be changed in settings. The page states it is free and open source, with no ads, tracking, or hidden costs.
notable: Works fully offline on the local network with no internet or account required
Cross-platform, including Windows, macOS, Linux, Android, and iOS
Optional PIN verification on top of HTTPS encryption
Described as an open-source alternative to AirDrop
caveats: Transfers only work between devices on the same local network, not over the internet
Speed is limited by the WiFi network, per the page
